title: Color Codes - Live Color Reference
body:
&CCOLOR CODES - LIVE COLOR REFERENCE&x

The names in this guide are actually displayed in their named colors.
The codes printed at left are literal text you can copy into a prompt.
Colors last until the next code; always finish with &&x to reset.

&WSTANDARD COLORS (uppercase code)&x
  &&R  &RRed&x                &&G  &GGreen&x
  &&Y  &YYellow&x             &&B  &BBlue&x
  &&C  &CCyan&x               &&M  &MMagenta&x
  &&W  &WWhite&x              &&D  &DDark gray&x

&WBRIGHT / BOLD COLORS (lowercase code)&x
  &&r  &rBright red&x         &&g  &gBright green&x
  &&y  &yBright yellow&x      &&b  &bBright blue&x
  &&c  &cBright cyan&x        &&m  &mBright magenta&x
  &&w  &wBright white&x       &&d  &dBright gray&x

&WEXTRAS&x
  &&O    &OOrange&x
  &&x    Reset to normal text

&W256-COLOR PALETTE&x
  &&[N] or &&N  Choose xterm color number N from 0 through 255.
  &&[196]  &[196]Bright xterm red&x    &&[208]  &[208]Orange&x
  &&[27]   &[27]Deep blue&x           &&[46]   &[46]Bright green&x
  &&[129]  &[129]Violet&x              &&[226]  &[226]Bright yellow&x
  &&O is a short alias for &&[208].
  Your client must support ANSI/256-color rendering to see these shades.

&WCOPYABLE EXAMPLES&x
  Type: prompt &&RHP:%h/%H &&BCH:%c/%C &&GST:%s/%S&&x
  Looks like: &RHP:100/120 &BCH:150/200 &GST:75/90&x
  Type: prompt &&[196]HP:%h/%H &&[39]CH:%c/%C&&x
  Looks like: &[196]HP:100/120 &[39]CH:150/200&x

&WIMPORTANT&x
  A single & followed by a valid code changes the color.
  Write &&&& to print a literal ampersand instead of changing color.
  Example: &&&&r displays literal &&r instead of changing the color.
  If you have disabled ANSI colors, the names still show in plain text.
  Also see HELP PROMPT for every usable prompt token and preset.
